# Writing a request-type spec

## Contents

- What "Proven" means
- The spec
- Fields
- Rules
- Limits the compiler enforces
- Not supported, and why
- The two opt-in gates
- Agreement Manager API names for the provisions
- Custom fields kept to a minimum (2026-10-28)
- Account-wide desk settings (`assets/desk-settings`)

This page is the reference for writing an Agreement Desk request type as a spec. It covers every key, binding, provision and limit. The compiler (`src/request-type-spec.ts`) turns a spec into the ZIP that **Requests ▸ Settings ▸ Request types ▸ Import** takes. The evidence for each rule is in [REQUEST_TYPES-CONFIG.md](REQUEST_TYPES-CONFIG.md). The form inside the package is a web form, so field properties follow [WEB_FORMS-CONFIG.md](WEB_FORMS-CONFIG.md) §4–5.

```bash
npx tsx captures/request-type-build.ts my-type.json --out out/                 # compile (offline); refuses a bad spec
DS_ACCOUNT=legacy npx tsx captures/request-type-verify.ts my-type.json        # prove it live (legacy, as "ZZ Lab · …")
```

## What "Proven" means

The **Proven** column uses three values:

- **yes** — the key appears in a library type whose current verify report passes. "Passes" means:
  - import reports Completed;
  - the form round-trips exactly;
  - the builder shows no error;
  - Create Request shows the field (`assets/request-types/verify/`).
- **web form only** — proven by the web-form verifier on a standalone form, never in a request form.
- **no** — compiles, never imported.

With `--submit` the verifier does submit a request and reads back what it stored (35/35 library types). An intake upload does not appear on the request's **Documents** tab (see `file` below).

## The spec

```jsonc
{
  "id": "nda-request",                     // file name, kebab-case
  "name": "NDA Request",                   // the picker tile; workflow triggers compare this
  "description": "Request a new NDA.",     // the line under the name
  "pages": [{ "title": "Request", "fields": [ /* … */ ] }],
  "rules": [ /* show/hide rules */ ]
}
```

| Key | Required | Meaning | Proven |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | yes | File name and seed for stable ids. Import mints new ids anyway. | yes |
| `name` | yes, non-empty | Tile name. A name already in the account imports as "… (1)". | yes |
| `description` | yes (may be `""`) | At most **400** characters (the picker's limit). | yes |
| `pages[]` | yes | One or more pages. All 35 library types and all 17 of the account's own forms are single-page. | single page: yes; two pages: import, round trip and builder only — page 2 never rendered |
| `pages[].title` / `subtitle` / `key` | title yes | `key` lets a rule show or hide the whole page. | title and subtitle: yes; page `key` as a rule target: imported (lab `zz-widgets`), its runtime effect not exercised |
| `pages[].fields[]` | yes | Fields, below. | |
| `rules[]` | no | Show/hide logic, below. | see Rules |
| `locale` | no | `en` (default) or `ja`, the only two locales measured. | no (all `en`) |

There is no Welcome page, review page, submit action or thank-you page. Create Request supplies the request-title box above the form and Submit below it. A web form's `hidden` prefill page is refused, because a request form has none.

## Fields

Every field has a `key`: letters, digits and `_`, unique across the form, including page keys. Most fields also have a `type` and a `bind`. The keys each type accepts are the web form's (`FIELD_KEYS` in `src/webform-spec.ts`). Anything else is refused.

| `type` | Extra keys | Proven |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `placeholder` `maxLength` `preset` (`zip`/`extendedZip`/`ssn`) `pattern` `default` | yes (`pattern`: imported in 5 types, never typed into; the others web form only) |
| `longtext` | `placeholder` `maxLength` `pattern` `default` | yes |
| `number` | `placeholder` `numberFormat` | yes (`numberFormat` web form only) |
| `currency` | `currency` (ISO, default `usd`) | yes (EUR/GBP web form only) |
| `date` | `placeholder` `dateFormat` (`MM_dd_yyyy` default, `dd_MM_yyyy`, `yyyy_MM_dd`) | yes (other formats web form only) |
| `email` | `placeholder` `maxLength` `default` | yes, stored as a bare string in a Text custom field (submit gate) |
| `phone` | `countryCode` (default `1`) `default` | yes, labs `zz-widgets` and `zz-props-submit`. Stored into a Text custom field as `{number, countryCode, normalizedNumber}` (Submit accepts the object) |
| `dropdown` | `options` | yes |
| `radio` | `options` | yes, labs `zz-widgets`, `zz-props-submit` (stored as the option value in a Text field) |
| `checkbox` | `options` `select` (`atLeast`/`atMost`/`exactly`) | yes (renders; `select` web form only) |
| `file` | `formats` `maxFileSizeInMB` (default 25) | renders, and a required upload submits (signature-request, marketing-review). Unbound. **The upload stays in the intake data and does NOT become a request document**: at Submit it is stored under `documents` as the file name, and the request's Documents tab (`GET …/tickets/{id}/documents`) stays empty (`--submit` on the lab account, 2026-10-28). Agents and workflow steps that read a request's documents never see it, so tell requesters to attach paper on the Documents tab after submitting |
| `description` | `text` (Markdown) | yes (builder; not checked in Create Request) |
| `section` | `label` `text` `fields` | yes, lab `zz-widgets` |

Every input type also takes `label`, `description` (help text), `required`, `readOnly` and `example`. `readOnly` is web form only; Docusign's Salesforce-launched form in the account uses it. `example` is a sample answer and never goes into the form.

`options` are strings or `{ label, value?, selected?, description? }`. The value is derived from the label and must be an identifier, so keep labels ASCII: no `$`, `£`, em dash or `;`. `selected` and option `description` are web form only.

**Help text on a provision date** replaces the date-format line the compiler writes otherwise. Docusign's own `[Example]` forms do this on Effective Date. It was proven live in lab `zz-date-help` (2026-10-24), and so was a `dd_MM_yyyy` provision date.

**Proven in a request form by lab `zz-widgets` (legacy, 2026-10-24).** These passed all five gates, and each showed in the Create Request picture:
- `phone` with `countryCode` (+44), `radio` stored as Text, `section`;
- `placeholder`, the `zip` preset, `readOnly` + `default`;
- `numberFormat` (comma), `currency: "eur"`;
- an option with `selected`, an option `description`, a page `subtitle`.

**In library types since 2026-11-02 (verify with `--submit --rules` queued):** `contract-termination` carries a section, a page
subtitle, a placeholder and `maxLength`, an option with `selected` and one with a `description`, `maxLineBreaks`, the Title,
ExecutionDate, Jurisdiction and TerminationDate provisions, and hide, `match: any`, `contains` and `isNot` rules;
`facility-lease` a text `default`, `numberFormat`, a `dd_MM_yyyy` provision date, AnnualValue and a radio; `employee-onboarding`
a radio, a checkbox `select` and file `formats` / `maxFileSizeInMB`. All bind provisions or pinned custom fields only.

A read-only field shows its default greyed out, with no "Read Only" badge (web forms show one). The rows below marked "web form only" for these keys are now proven by that lab, but not used by any library type.

### What a field is stored as: `bind`

A request stores the answer to a **bound** field. Bind every data field. Docusign's own forms do, and the library test enforces it. A field without `bind` renders, but whether its answer is kept is unmeasured.

```jsonc
{ "key": "counterparty", "bind": { "provision": "Party" }, "required": true }           // a Docusign field
{ "key": "owner", "type": "text", "label": "Business owner", "bind": { "custom": "BusinessOwnerName" } }
{ "key": "dept", "type": "dropdown", "options": ["Legal", "Sales"], "bind": { "custom": "IntakeDepartment", "label": "Requesting Department", "type": "Text" } }
```

#### Provisions

Provisions are Docusign's own fields. A provision field may omit `type` and `label`, which default to Docusign's. A provision dropdown takes Docusign's options; giving your own is refused. `GoverningLaw`, `Jurisdiction`, `EmploymentLocation` and `RenewalInfo` also accept `longtext`.

| `provision` | Field type | Docusign label | Options | Proven |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Party` | text → DynamicList (“Add another party”) | Party | — | yes — 28 library types |
| `Title` | text | Title | — | yes — lab `zz-props-submit` (submitted and stored) |
| `EffectiveDate` | date | Effective Date | — | yes — 17 library types |
| `ExecutionDate` | date | Execution Date | — | yes — lab `zz-props-submit` (submitted and stored) |
| `ExpirationDate` | date | Expiration Date | — | yes — 13 library types |
| `TotalValue` (alias `ContractValue`) | currency | Total Contract Value | — | renders in 20 library types. Submit with the old `ContractValue/value` path failed (400, abstract type); the fixed `TotalValue/value` path is unproven at Submit |
| `AnnualValue` | currency | Annual Contract Value | — | yes — lab `zz-props-submit` (EUR, submitted and stored) |
| `LiabilityCap` | currency | Limitation of Liability Cap | — | yes — 3 library types; stored value unproven |
| `PaymentTerms` | dropdown | Payment Terms | 11 Docusign options (`THIRTY_DAYS`…) | yes — 11 library types |
| `GoverningLaw` | text / longtext | Governing Law | — | yes — 2 library types |
| `Jurisdiction` | text / longtext | Jurisdiction | — | yes — lab `zz-props-submit` (submitted and stored) |
| `NdaType` | dropdown | NDA Type | One Way, Mutual | yes — 1 library types |
| `RenewalType` | dropdown | Renewal Type | Evergreen, Auto Renew, Renewal Option, Fixed Term | yes — 6 library types |
| `RenewalNoticeDate` | date | Renewal Notice Date | — | yes — 3 library types; stored value unproven |
| `RenewalInfo` | text / longtext | Additional Info | — | yes — 1 library types; stored value unproven |
| `EmploymentType` | dropdown | Employment Type | Full Time, Part Time, Intern, Fixed Term | yes — 2 library types |
| `EmploymentLocation` | text / longtext | Employment Location | — | yes — 2 library types |
| `HireDate` | date | Hire Date | — | yes — 2 library types |
| `TerminationDate` | date | Termination Date | — | yes — lab `zz-props-submit` (submitted and stored) |

Not available:
- **duration, percentage and yes/no provisions** (renewal notice period, late-fee %, late fees apply). They exist in the model, but no form in either account binds one, so their component shape is unknown.
- **any provision not in this table.** The full registry list is not in the repo.

The paths are written at `@1.5.0`. The account's older forms bind `@1.1.0`/`@1.3.0` and still render.

#### Custom fields

`{ "custom": "<Name>", "type"?, "label"?, "accountWideOptions"? }` stores into the account's custom field `C_<Name>`. Custom fields are **account-wide and hard to undo**: import creates or UPSERTs them, deleting the type leaves them, and no API removes them (an admin can delete one by hand in Agreement Manager ▸ Manage ▸ Fields (row ⋮ ▸ Delete; verified on Demo 2026-11-05), the public API cannot (DELETE custom-provisions answers 400), and values already extracted stay on agreements). So:

- **Name**: letters, digits and `_`, written WITHOUT `C_`.
- **Label**: the field's name in the account, not the question. It defaults to the name split at capitals (`RequestDescription` → "Request Description"). A different label for an existing field **renames it in every form** in the account. The library's set is pinned by name, label and type in `test/request-type-spec.test.ts`. Reuse a pinned field rather than adding one.
- **Type**: `Text`, `Number`, `Date`, `Dropdown` or `Currency`.

| Field `type` | Allowed custom `type` | If omitted |
|---|---|---|
| `text`, `longtext`, `email`, `phone` | `Text` | `Text` |
| `number` | `Number` only. A number is sent as a JSON number, and a Text field refuses it at Submit | `Number` |
| `currency` | `Currency` only. It writes the live model's exact shape (`MonetaryAmount` value, provision@1.5.0); compiled byte-for-byte equal to legacy's `C_TotalFees_dHeqcK`. **Proven:** lab `zz-currency-cf` (2026-10-25) submitted a currency answer into that field and it was stored. A Text field refuses a currency answer at Submit (400, 2026-10-25) | **refused — must be given** |
| `date` | `Date` only | `Date` |
| `dropdown` | `Dropdown` with `"accountWideOptions": true` (the library's choice), or `Text` | **refused — must be given** |
| `radio` | `Text` (options stay in the form). A radio on a `Dropdown` field is refused: Details shows its stored key | **refused — must be given** |
| `checkbox` | none: a checkbox bound to a custom field is refused. On Test 4 (2026-11-15) Submit failed 400 "Unexpected properties … `C_IntakeSubtype_…RestType`: value" for a checkbox on a new Text field, even with the pre-Dropdown spec and alone on a lab form; an unbound checkbox submits. Its answers stay in the intake data | — |
| `file`, `description`, `section` | none: these cannot be bound | — |

- **Choice questions use `Dropdown` fields** (2026-11-15). A request's Details tab shows a Dropdown field's option LABEL ("Fontara's paper"); a dropdown on a Text field shows the stored key ("Fontaras_paper"). Measured on Test 4, 2026-11-15 (lab probes A–J):
  - The import creates the field by name, with its options (`OptionKeys` = the option values, `Term_OptionValues` = the labels); Export carries it back the same way.
  - **A Dropdown field's option list is fixed once it exists.** An import that adds or drops an option fails whole (nothing is made). The import also gives every form the field's WHOLE list, in the field's order, so a form cannot show only some options. So a field is shared only by questions with the same list, and a new list needs a NEW field name. `test/request-type-dropdown-options.json` pins every list. A solution's request type that binds a library Dropdown field with another list is refused by the solution check (`dropdownClashes`, src/solution-check.ts): keep the library's list, or bind a field name of your own (a customer's entities: `<Company>DeskEntity`, not `DeskFontaraEntity`).
  - A Text field cannot become a Dropdown by import, not even after it is deleted (the name stays, deprecated). The library's Dropdown fields therefore have new names (`C_Desk*`) beside the older Text `C_Intake*` ones, which accounts loaded before keep.
  - The stored value is the option's value, as before. A request-started workflow gets the field as `<field>_selected` {value, label}, with no bare field (run 7b93e9a7); the workflow compiler rules on `_selected.label` and fills a template from `_selected.value`.
  - The Fields catalog (`GET {apps}/dcp-service/v1.0/accounts/{a}/catalog`, `dropdownOptions`) lists a field's option labels; the model does not. The import planners read it and refuse a load that would change a list ("reoption").
- `Table` is refused: it exists in the package format but was never seen on a form.
- **Submit gate** (`captures/request-type-verify.ts --submit`): fills the form, submits, and checks each bound field stores what was sent, then deletes the request. It found the two bugs above (abstract `ContractValue`; currency into Text). Email and phone answers stored in a Text field: being measured. A checkbox in a Text field fails Submit on a new account (above), so checkboxes are unbound.
- One field may be used by several types, but only with one definition. A package that defines it two ways is refused, because import keeps only one.
- **Within one form, a field appears once.** Two inputs bound to the same custom field or provision are refused. Docusign's release note of 17 Oct 2025 says "A field can appear only once on a request form". `ContractValue` and `TotalValue` count as one field. The three Renewal properties count as three.
- **Currency custom fields** are supported and proven. Fields Manager offers the type: the app's Agreement Desk bundle lists `Currency` among the components a request form can bind, and legacy holds one such field, `C_TotalFees_dHeqcK` ("Total fees"). Bind it with `{ "custom": "<Name>", "type": "Currency", "label": "<label in the account>" }` on a `currency` field. The compiler writes the live model's exact declaration: it was diffed byte-for-byte against the field read with `captures/recon-field-types.ts --dump`. Lab `zz-currency-cf` (legacy, 2026-10-25) passed all gates, including `--submit`: the answer was stored in the field. A currency answer in a Text field is still refused, because it fails at Submit.

## Rules

```jsonc
{ "when": [{ "field": "urgency", "is": "Urgent" }], "then": { "urgency_reason": "show" } }
```

- **Effects:** `show` or `hide` on a field, a section or a page `key`. Nothing else exists: `display` and `required` upload and do nothing.
- **`match`:** `all` (default) or `any` across the conditions.
- **Conditional "required":** `required: true` on the field plus a show rule. A hidden required field does not block Submit (lab `zz-props-submit`, 2026-10-25), as in web forms. The library still avoids it, so the library never makes a rule-revealed field required.
- **Party in a rule:** a rule may SHOW or HIDE Party (proven, lab `zz-party-rules`, 2026-10-24). It may NOT read Party: a `filled` rule on Party never fired in the same lab, so the compiler refuses Party as a condition.

**The allowed operators** are exactly what the builder's rule editor offers for each field type. Confirmed on a request intake form by `captures/recon-rule-operators.ts` (legacy, 2026-10-27). They are shared with web forms as `BUILDER_OPERATORS` in `src/webform-spec.ts`: harvested 2026-10-25 by `captures/recon-webform-properties.ts --only=operators`, and request forms use the same builder. The compiler refuses any other operator. Its message names the field, its type, the operator and the allowed list.

| Field type | Operators the builder offers | Proven in Create Request (`--rules`) |
|---|---|---|
| text, longtext, email | `filled`, `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `notContains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith` | `contains` → hide (zz-props-submit) |
| dropdown, radio, checkbox | `filled`, `is`, `isNot`, `isAnyOf`, `isNoneOf` | `is` (82 checks, 35 types), `isAnyOf` (open-source-review) |
| date | `filled`, `is`, `isNot`, `today`, `onOrBefore`, `onOrAfter`, `onDayOfWeek` | no |
| number, currency (incl. `TotalValue`, `AnnualValue`, `LiabilityCap`), phone, file | `filled` only | no |
| Party | the builder offers `filled` / not filled, but the compiler refuses Party as a condition: a `filled` rule on it never fired in Create Request (lab zz-party-rules) | — |

**No thresholds on amounts.** `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte` and date `before`/`after` do evaluate at run time: a `--rules` check saw currency `gt` fire. But the builder cannot show them, so nobody could open or edit such a rule, and the compiler refuses them. On 2026-10-27 the library's 13 threshold rules were removed:
- 12 were `value gt` (approver fields and CFO/priority notes in 10 types);
- 1 was order-form's `discount gt 30`.

Every one of their targets was optional and already states its threshold in its own text ("Over $100,000 total: …"), so it is now always shown. A band dropdown that routes by size would need a new permanent custom field and the owner's approval.


## Limits the compiler enforces

| Limit | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Description | ≤ 400 characters | REQUEST_TYPES-CONFIG §1 |
| Name | non-empty | — |
| Attachment (file) fields | ≤ 15 per form | Docusign Web Forms limits (hjv1686940185785), REQUEST-TYPES-GUIDE §4b |
| Components in one import | ≤ 44 (2 per type + 1 per distinct custom field) | 48 imported, 51 created nothing (REQUEST_TYPES-CONFIG §2); 44 is the safety margin |
| Keys | unique across fields and pages | a repeated key silently replaced the first field |
| Options | at least one; values are identifiers, unique | web-form builder and activation (WEB_FORMS-CONFIG §2, §4) |
| Rules | every condition and target names a field or page in the form | WEB_FORMS-CONFIG §7 |

## Not supported, and why

| Product feature | Why the spec cannot express it |
|---|---|
| **Inactive** or **Draft** type | Import ignores both. Measured 2026-10-25 (`captures/recon-request-type-state.ts`): a type file with `isEnabled: false`, `formState: "draft"`, or both, imported Completed as active and enabled, and was offered in Create Request. Deactivate it in Settings after import. |
| **Default** type (email intake) | Always `isDefault: false`. Setting it would take email intake from the account's current default, and import's handling is unmeasured. Set it in Settings ▸ ⋮ ▸ Set as default. |
| Statuses | Account-wide, exported and imported separately from types (REQUEST-TYPES-GUIDE §0.9). |
| Hidden prefill page | Web forms only. A request form has none (refused). |
| Number range and decimals; currency min/max and decimals; phone format | Docusign's help lists them, but the builder's Properties panel does not offer them (harvested by `captures/recon-webform-properties.ts`; request forms use the same builder). Defaults, the editable currency code and `maxLineBreaks` ARE offered and proven (below) |
| Duration, percentage and yes/no provisions | Component shape never observed (above). |
| Custom-field category (General, Renewal, Payment…) | Always "Other". A different category on an existing field would UPSERT it account-wide. Unmeasured. |
| `Table` custom field | Never seen on a form. |
| Unified fields (central field library) | The help calls them shared fields with a type, kept in the central field library and reused in Agreement Manager (tsk884f7dee). These are the account custom fields (`C_*`) this compiler binds. Not checked live: a `C_Intake*` field appearing as a Requests dashboard column. |
| Formula fields, scripted rules | Not offered by web forms. |
| Email/phone verification apps | Bound to one account's app instance; not portable. |

**Unverified lead.** Docusign's help agent (asked 2026-10-24; a lead, not proof) says the request-type builder offers only Text, Date, Dropdown, Number and Currency. The library's email, checkbox and file fields nonetheless import, pass the builder and render in Create Request. Phone, radio and section are the lab probe `zz-widgets`.


## The two opt-in gates

- `--submit`: fills Create Request, submits, and checks that each bound field stores what was sent, in both reads of the request. It then deletes the request and the Party records Submit made. It refuses unless Notifications and every active Agreement Desk workflow make a submit safe. All 35 library types pass.
- `--agreements` (with `--submit`): also reads the public Agreement Manager API, `GET https://api-d.docusign.com/v1/accounts/{acct}/agreements`, plus the request's own record if its ticket has a `navigatorAgreementId`. It is recorded only, never part of the verdict.
  - **A request is not an agreement.** On legacy (2026-10-25, msa-request and signature-request) the submitted request's `navigatorAgreementId` was `null`. The record appears when an agreement is created from the request, not at Submit.
  - The list answered 200, with 50 per page and a `_links.next.href` cursor.
- `--rules`: opens a fresh form for each rule, once with answers that make it true and once false, and checks that each target shows or hides accordingly. Page targets and conditions on rule-gated fields are skipped and listed. Six library types passed on 2026-10-25 (`is`, `isAnyOf`, `match: all`, description-note targets, and currency `gt`, which the compiler now refuses), as did `zz-props-submit` (`is`, `contains` → hide, `match: any`).

**Proven by `zz-props-submit`** (legacy, 2026-10-25, all seven gates): `default` on number, email, date (display format) and currency; `currencyEditable`; `maxLineBreaks`; `AnnualValue` in EUR (stored `{doubleValue, currencyCode: "EUR"}`).


## Agreement Manager API names for the provisions

Once a request has become an agreement, the public Agreement Manager API returns these provisions under snake_case keys. The keys below were read off the legacy account's agreement list (2026-10-25). The match to each provision is by name; it was not traced through a single record.

| `provision` | API key |
|---|---|
| `TotalValue` | `total_agreement_value + total_agreement_value_currency_code` |
| `AnnualValue` | `annual_agreement_value + annual_agreement_value_currency_code` |
| `LiabilityCap` | `liability_cap_fixed_amount (+ liability_cap_currency_code; also _multiplier, _duration)` |
| `EffectiveDate` | `effective_date` |
| `ExecutionDate` | `execution_date` |
| `ExpirationDate` | `expiration_date` |
| `GoverningLaw` | `governing_law` |
| `Jurisdiction` | `jurisdiction` |
| `PaymentTerms` | `payment_terms_due_date` |
| `RenewalType` | `renewal_type` |
| `RenewalNoticeDate` | `renewal_notice_date` |

Keys the API returns that no request-form provision binds yet: `term_length`, `auto_renewal_term_length`, `renewal_notice_period`, `termination_period_for_cause`, `termination_period_for_convenience`, `late_payment_fee_percent`, `can_charge_late_payment_fees`, `price_cap_percent_increase`, `assignment_type`, `assignment_change_of_control`. These are the durations, percentages and yes/no fields listed under "Not available" above.


## Custom fields kept to a minimum (2026-10-28)

The library binds **49** custom fields. Five were removed because the request or a standard field already holds them:
- `C_RequestorName` and `C_RequestorEmail`: the request records its submitter.
- `C_IntakeSubject`: the request title. Each form now says which name to put in the title box.
- `C_IntakeIncidentDate`: folded into the incident's details question.
- `C_IntakeEmployeeName`: a new hire or candidate is the agreement's Party. Legal-hold custodians moved into its details question.

Two candidates stay custom:
- `C_TargetDueDate`: the request's due date is not a property an intake field can write. No request due-date property appears among the fields a request exposes (Request Id, Title, Type, Status, Owner, Submitter, Created At). The intake form cannot write it. A request-started workflow can: Workflow Builder's Set Request Due Date step sets it On, Before or After a date, which can be a variable (help tskd40ee6bb), for example this field. Our workflow compiler writes only "N days after creation" today (an audit-workflows gap), so the field stays custom and is the source for that step.
- `C_IntakeTermMonths`: the `Term` provision is a Duration, and the request form builder's bindable components are TextBox, Date, Number, Select, DynamicList and Currency, with no Duration (app bundle `@iam/tasks`, read 2026-10-25).

Off legacy, `request-type-verify.ts --fields-only` lists the custom fields the specs need and which the account lacks; a run that would add any needs `--create-custom-fields`, which creates them ONCE, before the imports (`src/custom-field-setup.ts`). A field the account has with another label or type is never changed.

## Account-wide desk settings (`assets/desk-settings`)

What a request type cannot carry lives in one desk settings spec per account kind: `assets/desk-settings/specs/fontara-desk.json`
(`src/desk-settings.ts`). `captures/desk-settings.ts <spec>` plans (dry run), `--apply --account="<name>"` writes and reads back,
and a pass writes `assets/desk-settings/verify/<id>.json`. Keys: `defaultType` (Set as default; the type must be active),
`defaultStatus` (the top Open status), `deskAI` (Agreement Desk AI: type recommendation and form filling), `blockSendWhileApprovalsPending`,
`submitterConfirmation`, `submitterUpdates`, `newRequestNotification` (`{ to: ["self" | account user email] }` or `false`),
`externalMessages`, `externalSubmission`, `realTimeInvite` (Settings ▸ Email), and `requests` (the seed requests file, read back:
each request's last status, owner and approvals). The calls are the Requests app's own, listed in the script's header
(harvested on Test 4, 2026-11-10). Not settable anywhere: who may see a type's requests (no access control per type) and statuses
per type (statuses are account-wide); the request type compiler refuses `visibility`, `statuses` and `isDefault`.
